mechanism_narrative: A persistent increase in FEDFUNDS above 5% over two consecutive months signals a restrictive monetary policy stance, raising discount rates and reducing equity valuations, resulting in negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative (< -1%) in at least 70% of triggered episodes.

mechanism_narrative: A year-over-year decline in GDPC1 of more than 2% indicates weakening aggregate demand, which reduces corporate earnings expectations and leads to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly negative (< -2%) in at least 60% of triggered episodes.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained monthly increase in UNRATE above 4.0% for three consecutive months signals a tight labor market, which increases wage pressures and inflation, prompting the Fed to raise rates and resulting in negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative (< -1%) in at least 60% of triggered episodes.

mechanism_narrative: A monthly decline in INDPRO of more than 0.5% for two consecutive months signals weakening industrial production, which reduces corporate earnings and leads to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative (< -1%) in at least 60% of triggered episodes.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous monthly increase in HOUST and a decline in RSAFS signals rising housing demand but constrained supply, which historically precedes a short-term equity market pullback due to sector rotation, resulting in negative S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days.
candidate_trigger: HOUST > 0% and RSAFS < 0% in the same month
failure_condition: S&P 500 5-day forward returns are not significantly negative (< -0.5%) in at least 60% of triggered episodes.

mechanism_narrative: A coordinated rise in both FEDFUNDS and CPIAUCSL above their respective 12-month averages signals a dual shock of higher rates and inflation, which erodes real corporate earnings and leads to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS > 12-mo avg and CPIAUCSL > 12-mo avg in the same month
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly negative (< -2%) in at least 60% of triggered episodes.

mechanism_narrative: A monthly increase in PAYEMS above 0.4% for four consecutive months signals robust labor market expansion, which supports consumer spending and drives positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days regardless of regime.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly positive (> +1%) in at least 60% of triggered episodes.

mechanism_narrative: A monthly increase in GDPC1 above 0.5% coinciding with a decline in CPIAUCSL below 2.0% signals improving real demand without inflationary pressure, which historically supports equity valuations and produces positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: GDPC1 > 0.5% and CPIAUCSL < 2.0% in the same month
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly positive (> +1%) in at least 60% of triggered episodes.
